```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "Idea A's own brief cites a direct red flag: 100% churn of paying customers on a closely related SaaS. It also cites paid-parent reviews of Dinolingo describing children 'zoning out' on repetitive content. Both point at the core mechanic, not execution. Idea B's brief has no equivalent retention signal.",
    "Idea B's demand evidence is broader. It has three independent parent-side quotes describing the pain (tutoring too expensive, software not instructing well, trying many tools). Idea A has one parent quote, and its second quote is a competitor's marketing copy.",
    "Idea B's pricing is anchored by sourced price points across a wide range: free (Khan Kids), $14.99/mo (Ello), $119/yr (Synthesis), $500/mo (Mentava). This shows parents do pay in this category. Idea A's anchors are weaker: Voiczy's price is inferred from a gift-promo valuation, and KokoFun's price is not published.",
    "Idea A faces a competitor with an identical origin story and positioning (Voiczy). It also carries extra compliance weight from recording children's voices (COPPA biometric, GDPR-K). Idea B has COPPA obligations too, but its brief lays out a concrete, bounded mitigation (a one-time legal consult plus consent-record maintenance).",
    "Idea B targets a broader segment: all parents of 4–9 year-olds learning core skills. Idea A's 'expat parent teaching local language' niche is flagged by its own brief as possibly too small. A broader pool gives more room for organic community acquisition to produce a first paying customer within 90 days."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea A's demand evidence is the weakest part. The only real user quote is one r/expats parent who says they are 'considering online conversation classes or language programs.' That does not specifically signal demand for a self-serve vocabulary app, and arguably points toward live tutoring. The other 'demand' quote is Voiczy's own marketing copy, which is a competitor's sales claim, not independent customer evidence.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. Both briefs are thin on direct willingness-to-pay evidence from target customers, and neither shows conversion data for its organic channel. Idea B's organic-community channel cost is explicitly [unsourced]. Idea B also faces a fully free, well-resourced incumbent (Khan Academy Kids) that could cap pricing, and its brief names no clear differentiation. B wins mainly because A carries an explicit 100% churn red flag and weaker demand sourcing, not because B's case is strong."
}
```
